# legacy2mcp

> legacy2mcp turns a legacy SOAP/WSDL service, a database (Postgres, SQL Server, or Oracle), or a REST API into a typed, schema-validated, audit-logged MCP (Model Context Protocol) server, with no hand-written adapter code.

## Core capabilities

- SOAP: introspects a live WSDL with `zeep` and builds a JSON Schema per operation; every call is validated against it before it reaches the SOAP endpoint.
- Database: introspects a live Postgres/SQL Server/Oracle schema and exposes `select_<table>` / `insert_<table>` tools for an explicit table allowlist, plus named parameterized queries. There is no path from the LLM to arbitrary SQL, ever.
- REST: builds tools from an explicit endpoint allowlist, either hand-written or generated by `legacy2mcp init` (which can discover a live OpenAPI/Swagger spec from a URL, or statically scan a GitHub repo's routes/models).
- Write-like operations (SOAP write-verb names, DB inserts, non-GET REST endpoints) are excluded by default and require `allow_write_operations: true` set explicitly.
- Every tool call is audit-logged as one JSON line (tool, arguments, timestamp, outcome). Arguments are logged as-is: no PII redaction and no encryption at rest yet.

## Install and run

```bash
pip install legacy2mcp
legacy2mcp init --rest-url "https://your-api.example.com" --out config.yaml   # or --wsdl-url / --github-url
legacy2mcp inspect --config config.yaml   # review the generated tools
legacy2mcp run     --config config.yaml   # start the MCP server (stdio)
```
